title: Do Physicians Improve More from Positive or Negative Feedback?
eligible_reason: Single adoption date: the ProPublica Surgeon Scorecard release (post indicator, one date in 2015) for all surgeons; the DiD compares physicians receiving positive vs negative feedback (i.post##i.positive_own / positive_peer) with patient and physician controls (adjcomplicationrate i.zone tot_numpeers age female hispanic mscore rscore black medicare commercial) and hospital/procedure/zip FE; quarter-by-valence event-time interactions (ib14.time##i.positive_own); RDD on the report-card threshold. Not staggered; controls in all columns. Physician encounter data (final_analytic_Mar2023, placebo_final, MS_RNR_rdd) are not in the package.
design_notes: Package 'Replication Package 1.1': Physician Analysis/ (read_me.rtf, run_all.do, code/Tab1-2, TabA1-A6, Fig2-3, FigA2-A8 .do files, output/*.tex and .ster, log/logoutput_all.log) and Experimental Analysis/ (two .dta files with lab-experiment data and two .do files). Only the experimental data are shipped; the clinical data are referenced via $anly_input and absent.
data_access: proprietary (clinical encounter data not shipped); experimental data public
screener_notes: Flags for Callaway, Sun-Abraham, Goodman-Bacon are citations; no such estimators in code.
